title: Laws of Cricket - 1809 Code (Wallis broadsheet of 25 May 1809)
publisher_or_author: Association of Cricket Statisticians and Historians (reproducing the text by permission of MCC)

title: Raw OCR title pages and colophons of the dataset's 1774-1820 editions
reliability_note: Identifies the printings used: 1774 'New LAWS &c. Of The Game of Cricket'; 1786 'LAWS, &c' ending 'END of the NEW LAWS' followed by the 1755 code; 1803 R. Pocock, Gravesend; 1806 J. Bailey, Chancery Lane (undated); 1809 J. Baxter, Lewes; 1816 and 1820 T. Craft (MCC printer). Raw OCR also used to check numbers and cleaning artefacts.

title: Laws of Cricket - 1829 Code
publisher_or_author: Association of Cricket Statisticians and Historians (reproducing MCC text by permission of MCC)
reliability_note: Fetched 2026-10-27. Independent transcription of the official MCC code of 1829 (Laws 1-43, double-wicket only; no single-wicket or bets section). Uses 'run' throughout (no 'notch'), 'from a stroke of the bat, or hand (but not wrists)', 'One Short', 'The umpires shall enforce this law', 'stop the ball with his hat ... five runs', stumps 27 in/bails 8 in with thickness clause, bowling crease 6 ft 8 in 'towards the bowler at right angles'. Already contains the May 1828/1829 No-ball and Wide amendments, so not a witness for those, but a reliable witness for the unchanged laws either side of the 1828 Sporting Magazine text.

title: The 1820 Laws of Cricket (broadsheet printed by T. Craft) reproduced in facsimile

type: independent transcription (facsimile; OCR of the plate in the Rait Kerr text file)
reliability_note: Facsimile (about one-third scale) of the official 1820 broadsheet; OCR in the local text file at lines ~1563-1695 is noisy but legible. Independent of the project's 1820 typescript. Shows 'by rolling, watering, covering, mowing, or beating: This rule is not meant to prevent...', 'when the Ball is delivered' in the No-ball law, and LBW 'shall have pitched in a straight line'.

title: Data appendix of the rule-text dataset (Data Cleaning by Year rows 1828/1830/1835; Data Cleaning Heuristics row 10)
reliability_note: States that the 1830 text is a 'Single Year' rulebook which 'does not have the changes recorded as having been made for 1830', and that the 1835 text is a composite: main Laws from the second of two versions in the 1835 PDF, single-wicket and bets sections from the first version. Says nothing about the dating of the second version.

title: Laws of Cricket - 1829 Code
publisher_or_author: ACS (Association of Cricket Statisticians and Historians) reproducing MCC text
reliability_note: Fetched 2026-10 via a summarising fetch tool, not transcribed by hand. Laws 1-43 only (no single wicket or bets). Confirms the official 1829 wording: bowling crease 6 ft 8 in with return crease at each end; wickets pitched by the umpires; after-rain law (Law 8); No ball law 'The ball shall be bowled' with hand/arm above the elbow a No ball (Law 10); wide recorded as a wide (Law 12); no-ball penalty of one run when no run is otherwise obtained (Law 13); hit wicket by dress (Law 23); LBW ball 'delivered' in a straight line, any part of person (Law 25); substitutes Law 33 with umpire enforcement; stumps of sufficient thickness (Law 3). No provenance note beyond 'by kind permission of MCC'.

title: Circular of the M.C.C. Secretary (Lord's Cricket Ground 20 March 1835) with 'The Laws of Cricket revised by the Marylebone Club in the Year 1835' (proposed revision; new parts in italics)
reliability_note: Raw OCR of the first of the two versions in the project's 1835 scan; italics marking the new parts are lost in OCR and pages with Laws 38-42 are partly illegible. It is the proposal put to the Anniversary of 14 May 1835, not the adopted text (e.g. it has a 4 ft 4 in popping crease and a 9 1/8 in ball limit that were not adopted), so it dates wording to the 1835 revision but does not prove adoption.

title: History of the Laws of Cricket (continued), Laws 16-25, in Cricket: A Weekly Record of the Game, 28 Feb 1901, p.21
type: secondary historical (contemporary serial history of each 1884-code Law)
reliability_note: Fetched 2026-10 via the ACS archive. States that on May 2nd 1850 the M.C.C. settled that leg byes should be marked separately in the score 'so that it could be seen how much in fault the long stop might be', and that byes were not in the Laws until 1884. Taylor's dates sometimes differ from Rait Kerr (S16).

title: History of the Laws of Cricket (continued), Laws 26-43, in Cricket: A Weekly Record of the Game, 28 Feb 1901, p.22
type: secondary historical (contemporary serial history of each 1884-code Law)
reliability_note: Fetched 2026-10 via the ACS archive. Substitutes (restriction on where they may field said to last until 'May 15th, 1845' - Rait Kerr dates the consent change May 15th 1854, so Taylor's year may be a misprint); lost ball ('or recovered' said to have done away with many disputes); before 1884 the fieldsman penalty concerned stopping the ball with his hat, widened in 1884; first mention of a batsman infringing the obstruction law in 1864. Summarised by a fetch tool, not transcribed by hand.

title: History of the Laws of Cricket, Laws 1-11, in Cricket: A Weekly Record of the Game, 31 Jan 1901, p.16
type: secondary historical (contemporary serial history of each 1884-code Law)
reliability_note: Fetched 2026-10 via the ACS archive. Gives the 1884-code wicket as 8in wide with two bails of 4 inches each (independent check on the processed 1884 text, whose '4¾in.' bail length is not in the raw OCR); rolling-before-each-day's-play rule first applied 1883; over-arm fully allowed 1864. Summarised by a fetch tool, not transcribed by hand.

title: Addenda: Alteration of Law No. 10 by the Marylebone Club, May 1858 (in The Laws of Cricket for Single and Double Wicket, Toronto: Henry Rowsell, 1857)

title: The Laws of Cricket, 16th edition (with authorised decisions and interpretations): preface and Laws with inline '(Introduced/Revised <date>)' tags
publisher_or_author: MCC (preface signed R S Rait Kerr, Secretary)
type: primary (MCC publication; raw OCR of the scanned 1939 edition used by this dataset)
reliability_note: Primary MCC text. The preface says the edition was 'rendered necessary by changes in the Laws of the game, in the Rules governing International and County Cricket, and by additions to the notes, interpretations and other details', and that the notes were lettered and sub-divided and an index added; it states the aim of the whole edition, not the cause of any one note. Each Law carries the dates of its alterations since 21 April 1884, which date changes but do not explain them. The same book places the 'first-class fixture' note under Classification of Counties (outside the dataset's Laws text).

title: The Laws of Cricket, 15th edition (with decisions and interpretations authorized by the M.C.C.): preface, inserted slip 'Alterations of Laws 24 and 41', and 'Alterations and additions ... for matches overseas'
type: primary (MCC publication; raw OCR of the scanned 1932 edition used by this dataset)
reliability_note: Primary MCC text. Preface: edition needed 'by changes in the Laws of the Game ... and by additions to notes, interpretations and other details'; quotes Lacey that the notes answer the 'hundreds of cases' sent to the M.C.C. for decision each year (aim of the whole publication, not the cause of one note). Title page: Laws 'as revised ... 1884 ... 1927, 1928 & 1931'. The slip dates the new Laws 24 and 41 (Special General Meetings of 5 May 1937 and 6 May 1936). The overseas section (Law 9 rolling, eight-ball over for Australia/NZ, 200-run follow-on for Australia) and the instructions sections (The Batsman, The Bowlers, The Boundary, Umpires, Code of Signalling) are in the book but were not segmented into the dataset's Laws.

title: The Laws of Cricket, 14th edition (revised to 1922), including an inserted 'Note on Law 21' recording an M.C.C. Committee decision of 15 June 1931
type: primary (MCC publication; raw OCR of the scanned edition used as the dataset's 1923 text)
reliability_note: Primary MCC text, a multi-year publication (title page: Laws as revised up to 1920 & 1922). The data appendix removed the 1931 insert from the processed 1923 text. Its instructions sections (Notice to Umpires, The Batsman, The Bowlers, The Boundary, Umpires, signalling) are not segmented into the dataset's Laws.

title: Data appendix: data cleaning by year (1923/1932/1939 rows)
reliability_note: Documents which parts of each scanned book were kept: 1923 drops a 1931 note on Law 21; 1932 drops the overseas alterations and the 1936/1937 slip; 1939 drops the preface and everything from the Imperial Cricket Conference section on. Explains several segmentation artefacts in these pairs.

title: Revised Laws of Cricket: the M.C.C. draft (London cable of 7 January 1947, reporting The Times)
publisher_or_author: Evening Star (Dunedin), also Otago Daily Times and Chronicle (Levin), via Papers Past (National Library of New Zealand)
type: secondary contemporary press (wire reprint of a Times report on the MCC draft Code)
reliability_note: LOW/UNVERIFIED: the page returned empty content to WebFetch and a direct download was refused (bot check), so the text was NOT read. Content known only from two web-search result summaries (2026-10-27): the draft would no longer treat a wicket as down merely because a bail was dislodged; a bail lodging between two stumps counts as down; the bails were to be shortened by an eighth of an inch and the stump tops made dome-shaped (apart from the grooves) to prevent bails jamming; the revised Laws would not operate until the 1948 English season; the last over to be played out at the request of either captain. Not to be quoted. Same report also at https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/ODT19470108.2.62

title: Wisden's Answers To Cricket Queries
type: secondary contemporary press (reprint of Wisden material)
reliability_note: LOW/UNVERIFIED: not fetched (Papers Past returns empty content to automated fetches). Known only from a web-search result summary (2026-10-27) saying it reprints Wisden's explanation that the old last-over rule let the batting side use the two-minute window to its advantage and that the either-captain option applies only at the end of a match. Supplementary to Rait Kerr (S16) only; not to be quoted.
